name: [[498,83,30]] mirror fold (symplectic halving) of a [[996,166]] pair-partition CPM code

provenance.construction: Symplectic halving (mirror fold) of an unpublished [[996,166]] CSS code of ours (5 x 12 pair-partition CPM template of Okada and Kasai, arXiv:2607.14091, prime lift P = 83, check weight 8; same 5 x 12 template and column pairing as our board entry codes/996-166-34.json, with different circulant exponents; lightest logical found 36, upper bound). The fold uses the fixed-point-free involution tau(l,t) = (sigma(l), b_l - t mod 83) on parent qubit l*83+t, sigma = [1, 0, 3, 2, 5, 4, 7, 6, 9, 8, 11, 10] (block columns), b = [0, 0, 76, 76, 53, 53, 27, 27, 32, 32, 68, 68]; it maps the parent X-check row space onto the Z-check row space (this is the halving map pi(l,t) = (sigma(l), eta(t + beta_l)) with eta = -1 of arXiv:2609.30069). Fold qubit i is the pair {q_i, tau(q_i)}, q_i the i-th smallest qubit with q_i < tau(q_i). Each parent X-check row gives one generator: X on the pairs whose q_i is in the row, Z on the pairs whose tau(q_i) is in the row (both = Y). S = (A|B) is isotropic, k = 166/2 = 83, check weight 8, not CSS under any local Clifford (the verifier check stabilizer_code_is_not_locally_css passes).
provenance.notes: Derived from an unpublished [[996,166]] CSS code of ours (5 x 12 pair-partition CPM template of Okada and Kasai, arXiv:2607.14091, prime lift P = 83, check weight 8; same 5 x 12 template and column pairing as our board entry codes/996-166-34.json, with different circulant exponents; lightest logical found 36, upper bound), by @MicheldeMessieres. The halving/doubling correspondence and the CPM halving map are Prop. 4 and Sec. on halving of arXiv:2609.30069 (board fieldnote fieldnotes/2026-09-28-symplectic-doubling-and-halving.md, @MathysRennela); mirror codes of Khesin and Lu (arXiv:2603.05496); the reverse-fold shape (l,t) -> (l+5,-t) on a circulant parent is that of @MinboGaoTHU's codes/485-97-25.json, and his parent-symmetry witness transfer (used in his distance revision of @jacksongquera's codes/480-12-34.json) is the same idea as our shift-scored search. Our part, stated narrowly: the parent code, the choice of its one X<->Z mirror, and the distance search: Stern information-set decoding on the parent with pair-aware information sets, every logical found scored as a fold logical under all 83 cyclic shifts, plus a Pauli-weight Stern search on the fold itself; 16.50 CPU-h, 8958796 iterations. Distance d = 30 is the Pauli weight of the lightest logical found: a witness-backed upper bound, not a certificate. Construction and literature novelty are not claimed.
